name: Jena optical-glass supply
summary: A Jena glass laboratory began supplying many new optical glasses, including borate and phosphate types, giving lens designers far more combinations of bending and colour-spreading power.
description: The Jena Glastechnisches Laboratorium supplied a wider selection of optical glasses, including borate and phosphate compositions with varied refractive-index and dispersion combinations.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Microscope designers could not correct colour errors fully with the few glass types then available.

date.basis: Zeiss states the Jena new glasses had been used in its objectives since 1886.

events.statement: Zeiss reported that it used the new Jena glass in its microscope objectives from 1886.
events.population: Zeiss optical workers making microscope objectives in Jena
events.caveats: The source establishes use in the Jena firm, not the first outside glass sale or the use of every specified glass formulation.

evidence.locator: printed p. 1 / PDF p. 5, first paragraph
evidence.supports: The firm explicitly reports using the new material in objectives since 1886.

links.statement: Abbe says that the measured composition–optical-property relations guided glass syntheses and that the Jena supply operation resulted from these experiments.
links.scope: Schott–Abbe program and Jena optical-glass manufacture reported in 1886.
links.alternatives: Empirical workshop glassmaking long preceded this program; the claim concerns its particular expanded material range.
links.caveats: Abbe’s participant account gives a program-level sequence rather than melt-by-melt industrial records.
links.timing: The program began in 1881 and continued as production developed; the 1886 supply endpoint is an attestation within the overlapping research interval.
